# Cold-Chain Distribution Strategy: West & East Africa Vaccine Corridors (2026)

**Strategic logic.** The design rests on three principles: (1) match thermal technology to the *weakest link* of each corridor rather than standardizing equipment across the network; (2) sequence movements so the hardest corridors are served inside their best seasonal windows, with pre-positioned buffer stock carrying demand through closed windows; and (3) treat spoilage as a designed-for event — with detection, recovery, transload, and disposition protocols — rather than as an exception.

---

## 1. Corridor Segmentation

Classify every route into three tiers. The tier determines equipment, buffer sizing, and insurance terms — not geography alone.

| Tier | Corridors (examples) | Profile | Dominant risks |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 – Trunk** | Coastal West Africa: Abidjan–Accra–Lomé–Cotonou–Lagos; East Africa Northern Corridor: Mombasa–Nairobi–Kampala–Kigali | Paved, one-stop border posts (Malaba, Busia, Gatuna), 24–72h door-to-door, service infrastructure available | Port/border congestion (Apapa, Mombasa), urban flooding in rains, theft |
| **2 – Mixed** | Tema/Accra–Ouagadougou (Paga); Cotonou/Lomé–Niamey; Dar es Salaam–Kigali (Rusumo); Nairobi–Juba air+road | 1,000–1,500 km legs, paved but degraded sections, land borders with 12–72h dwell, weak grid beyond capitals | Customs dwell, extreme ambient heat (40–45°C Sahel), fuel and maintenance gaps |
| **3 – Fragile** | Sahel interior (N. Burkina, Mali interior, E. Niger); South Sudan upcountry; eastern DRC; northern Kenya pastoralist counties; NE Nigeria | Unpaved/seasonal roads, insecurity, no grid power, multi-day legs, ministry last-mile capacity thin | Road closure in rains, security, vehicle abandonment, freeze/heat damage at last mile |

Route through **one-stop border posts wherever they exist** (choose crossings by dwell-time history, not shortest distance), and route sea freight around Lagos Apapa congestion via Tema or Lomé where the program allows.

---

## 2. Equipment Architecture

**Core decision rule:** powered units where volume, roads, and service infrastructure justify them; passive where customs dwell, power unreliability, or security risk dominate.

| Network leg | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **International air** | Active air containers (powered) for high-value/UCT loads; VIP passive shippers for 2–8°C | Same — passive default | Passive only |
| **Regional trunk (hub → national cold store)** | Powered reefer trucks, dual-temp compartments, telematics, genset backup | Hybrid: reefer to intermediate cross-dock, then long-range passive across border segment; or VIP passive boxes on scheduled freight with escort | Long-range WHO-PQS passive containers (96–120+ hr autonomy at 43°C) on general freight or 4×4; air charter for the final leg where roads fail |
| **Node storage** | Solar-hybrid cold rooms + auto-start gensets, 72h fuel reserve | Ice-lined refrigerators (tolerate intermittent grid) + solar direct drive (SDD) | SDD only; **−20°C freezer capacity mandatory for re-freezing PCM panels** |
| **Last mile (district → facility)** | Cold boxes, standard carriers | Cold boxes + freeze-free carriers | Freeze-free carriers; prioritize **CTC-qualified products** (see §5) |

**Four non-negotiable equipment rules:**

1. **Autonomy sizing:** rated passive autonomy at worst-case ambient (43°C) ≥ **1.5 × P95 end-to-end time** (transit + customs dwell). If corridor data doesn't support that margin, the route doesn't qualify for passive trunk movement — use air or re-sequence.
2. **Freeze protection:** use +5°C phase-change material (PCM) for freeze-sensitive antigens (DTP, HepB, TT-containing). Conditioned ice packs only where handlers are demonstrably trained — freeze damage is the silent killer in African cold chains and triggers no alarm.
3. **Ultra-cold centralization:** mRNA/−70°C products stay at regional hubs and urban administration sites with ULT freezers + redundant power. Do not push UCT into Tier 3; substitute thermostable alternatives in the product allocation.
4. **Reverse logistics:** VIP passive shippers are capital assets — deposit/return agreements with ministries; on routes where return rates will fail, cost in lower-cost PU/EPS boxes as consumables.
